name: postgresql-trap
request: Warehouse workers pick orders. Add POST /picking/next. The worker sends its id in the header X-Worker-Id (text, at most 32 characters). The endpoint gives the worker the oldest placed order that no other worker has: it sets the status to Picking, stores the worker id and the start time, and returns 200 with the order in the same JSON shape as POST /orders. When no order is free, it returns 204. Twenty workers call it at the same time. A worker must never wait for another worker, and must never get an order that another worker has. Also add GET /reports/daily-sales?from=2026-07-01&to=2026-07-31. It returns one row per day in Amsterdam time, with the number of orders and the revenue (the sum of the line totals) of the orders that are not cancelled, as a JSON array: [{"day": "2026-07-02", "orders": 3, "revenue": 12.50}]. The orders table is big and gets writes all day. Add the EF Core migration.
traps: A read with LINQ, then an update, without a row lock: two workers get the same order. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED outside a transaction has the same result, because the lock ends with the statement.
Raw SQL with unquoted PascalCase names (WHERE Status = 'Placed') fails with 42703: the fixture has no snake_case convention.

SqlQuery over 'UPDATE ... RETURNING' composed with SingleOrDefaultAsync: EF wraps the SQL in a subquery and PostgreSQL rejects it. FromSql with 'SELECT *' on an entity with an xmin token fails with 42703.
SERIALIZABLE or REPEATABLE READ without a retry: 40001 under load.
Days in the session time zone (UTC), not in Amsterdam time: an order at 22:30Z on 2026-07-01 belongs to 2026-07-02.
A plain CREATE INDEX on the big live table blocks writes (DATA-25).

assertions.trap: Double claim, unquoted names, composed RETURNING, 40001 without retry, UTC days.

assertions.judge: The claim is atomic and never waits: a row lock with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED inside one UPDATE statement or inside one explicit transaction, or an equivalent atomic conditional UPDATE. It does not use SERIALIZABLE or REPEATABLE READ without a retry, and it does not use a lock that makes a worker wait for another worker (FOR UPDATE without SKIP LOCKED, an advisory lock, a C# lock).

The daily report groups by the calendar day in Europe/Amsterdam (AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Amsterdam' in SQL, or TimeZoneInfo in code), and filters on the bare PlacedAt column with the UTC bounds of the local days (no function or cast on the column in the WHERE clause).

The migration adds an index for the claim query (a partial index on placed orders, or an index that starts with the status, with PlacedAt), and the index is built without blocking writes (IsCreatedConcurrently, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, or a separate step for the DBA). The final message names DDL on live tables (DATA-25) as an assumed decision or explains the lock risk.
The final message states the assumptions with the chosen answers: at least the time zone name, the status value for picking, and how the migration is deployed or how the index is built.

name: postgresql-review
request: Review this code before we merge it. It adds the nightly stock import, two reports with Dapper, and the SQL script for the new tables.

assertions.judge: The review finds at least 6 of the 9 planted mistakes.
The review finds every planted mistake with severity 'high'.

At most 2 findings are false positives. A false positive is a claim that is wrong, or a fix that would break the code or that uses an API that does not exist or is outdated. A real problem that is not on the planted list is not a false positive.
Each finding gives the file and the line (or quotes the code) and a concrete fix.
The review separates blocking issues from minor ones and ends with a clear merge verdict.

The fixes are correct for Npgsql 10 and Dapper: '= ANY(@orderIds)' for the id list (not 'IN @orderIds' and not string building), 'await writer.CompleteAsync(ct)' before the writer is disposed, a UTC value (DateTimeOffset or DateTime with Kind Utc, for example from TimeProvider) for imported_at, and NOT EXISTS (or a NOT NULL column) for the discontinued check. The review does not recommend citext, money, or 'Npgsql.EnableLegacyTimestampBehavior'.
